name: fun
title: What Did Cavemen Do For Fun? (A 35,000-Year-Old Flute!)

lines: Someone in the Stone Age made a flute from a vulture's wing bone.
And it's at least thirty-five thousand years old.
So what did cavemen do for fun?
Meet Moss. He's bored.
Surprise one: music.
Found in Hohle Fels cave, Germany, it has five finger holes.
Experts carved a copy from vulture bone.
And yes, it plays.
Surprise two: kids' doodles.
In Rouffignac cave, France, over thirteen thousand years ago, children dragged fingers through soft clay.
Some lines reach the ceiling.
Scientists think grown-ups lifted them up.
Surprise three: tiny hands.
In Spanish caves, maybe a quarter of hand outlines are children's.
Paint was blown around a hand on the wall.
Like a Stone Age selfie.
Surprise four: stories.
Among Kalahari hunter-gatherers today, most long fireside chats at night are stories.
There's singing and dancing too.
It's a modern clue, but a lovely one.
So Stone Age fun sounds like ours.
Music. Messy art. A really good story.
And Moss? Still can't play the flute.
Follow for more Stone Age Stories.
